description: The only operations that require a human decision. Everything not listed here is expected to proceed autonomously inside a reviewed merge request. Asking humans to approve routine work is a defect in this policy, not a safety feature.

human_approval_required.why: Commits the organization to long-lived constraints.
Adds permanent operational and hiring cost.
Accepts residual risk on the organization's behalf.
Breaks consumers outside this repository's control.
Destroys shared history or bypasses review.

human_approval_required.category: change to this repository's hooks, policies or agent permissions

human_approval_required.why: The requester confirming that what was written is what they meant. No predicate can decide this: it is the ground truth every later definition of done derives from. It was the one gate in the workflow with no policy reference, so the most load-bearing human decision in the lifecycle left no machine-readable record.

Releasing with known unmet test criteria. Distinct from AP-09: approving a merge is not accepting that something is knowingly untested. The simulation previously recorded this decision as AP-09, which filed a quality judgement under a branch-protection id.

Authorizing deployment now, against production as it currently stands. AP-01 approves what is in the release; this authorizes acting on it. Both acts previously carried AP-01, so the second was already satisfied by the first and the separation the design argues for existed only in prose.

A change request alters something the organization already promised. The assessment says what it costs; only a human says whether that is worth paying. Distinct from AP-03: selecting a technology is a different decision from changing a target the current technology already meets.

explicitly_autonomous: creating and pushing a feature, defect or hotfix branch
opening and updating a merge request
writing, refactoring and testing code inside an approved story
running builds, tests, linters and static analysis
authoring requirements, architecture, test and documentation artifacts for review
responding to review comments and fixing CI failures
read-only investigation of logs, metrics and traces

mechanism.in_session: Hooks return permissionDecision "deny" for prohibited actions and "escalate" for actions that need a human decision, so Claude Code prompts the operator instead of silently proceeding.
mechanism.out_of_session: Merge request approval in GitLab, recorded by a named human. Agents never approve their own work.
mechanism.limits: Claude Code cannot bind a human approval to a later action. Approval granted for one command does not carry to the next. Durable approval lives in GitLab, not in the session.
